_comment: Precedent jurisdictions and impact research. Sourced largely from the owner's 'Data Center Research' bookmarks. These shape which criteria appear in the DP checklist — they document where these applications actually get contested.
intro: Alberta's municipal regime is young. Loudoun County, Virginia has the most mature data centre zoning framework anywhere and has already worked through the conflicts Alberta municipalities are now meeting for the first time. The impact research below is what turns a generic checklist into one that asks the questions residents will ask.

jurisdictions.name: Loudoun County, Virginia
jurisdictions.why: The largest data centre concentration in the world and the most developed municipal standards. Its use-specific standards are the closest thing to a tested template for what a data centre bylaw should contain.
lessons: Use-specific standards separate from the base zoning district
Explicit height, setback and buffer requirements tied to adjacent residential uses
Noise standards measured at the property line, not the equipment
Substation and transmission infrastructure treated as part of the application, not a separate matter
Design and screening standards to address the visual mass of large windowless buildings

jurisdictions.name: Virginia — JLARC legislative study
jurisdictions.why: A legislature's own independent review of the data centre industry's effects: electricity demand, ratepayer impact, tax incentives, land use and water. Rare as an evidence base not produced by industry or by opponents.
lessons: Quantified the ratepayer cost question rather than leaving it rhetorical
Assessed whether tax incentives delivered the promised returns
Modelled electricity demand growth against generation build rates
